title: Cygnus Tech - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Initial discovery for a Private/VPC deployment. Focus on network connectivity options (VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints, transit gateway), region constraints for data residency, egress IPs, audit/logging, and KMS integration. AE+SE from Redwood presented architecture options, asked about Cygnus networking constraints and timeline. Agreed next steps: share architecture doc, pricing matrix, sample Terraform network template, and schedule a technical deep dive for security engineering.
next_steps: Jordan Patel: Send private deployment architecture doc and pricing matrix
Samira Chen: Share Terraform network template and runbook
Nina Alvarez: Supply CIDR ranges, existing transit gateway details, and compliance checklist
Schedule technical deep dive with Cygnus security team (proposed week of 2026-11-22)
action_items: Jordan Patel: Email architecture + dedicated pricing - due 2026-11-20
Samira Chen: Share example VPC peering and PrivateLink templates - due 2026-11-22
Nina Alvarez: Provide internal CIDR ranges and any blocked IP lists - due 2026-11-18
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Samira, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hi Jordan, hey Samira, good thanks. I'm Liam, head of platform at Cygnus. We also have Nina from security and Ethan our CTO.
[00:20] Jordan Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda, we want to understand your networking constraints for private deployment, whether you prefer VPC peering or private endpoints, region constraints for data residency, and any audit/KMS needs. Also timeline and success criteria.
[00:35] Ethan Park: Great. To start, we are exploring Redwood for inference serving but everything must run in our VPC in AWS, no public internet egress for inference traffic. So private endpoints or peering is required.
[00:48] Samira Chen: Understood. Do you have a preference between VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink/Private endpoints? They trade off different things — peering is simpler sometimes but PrivateLink gives you private IPs without peering limits.
[01:02] Nina Alvarez: Our security team prefers PrivateLink because it isolates the service behind an endpoint and we can control endpoint policies, but we also need predictable egress IPs for our outbound firewall rules.
[01:15] Liam O'Connor: Also, we have multi-account setup with a central transit gateway. We generally route all vendor traffic through the transit gateway and egress via a set of NAT gateways with static Elastic IPs. Would Redwood be able to route through a transit gateway?
[01:30] Samira Chen: Yes, we can support transit gateway peering or a VPC-to-VPC peering model. For PrivateLink, you'd create an endpoint in your VPC that talks to our service endpoint. If you're routing through TGW, we would need the endpoint to be reachable from the accounts behind the TGW; sometimes that requires endpoint policies and route table entries.
[01:48] Jordan Patel: To add, our Private deployment runs a private control plane in your VPC and an inference plane on customer-managed subnets. That gives you full network isolation and you control the egress path.
[01:59] Ethan Park: When you say 'private control plane' — is that a managed service that still calls back to Redwood over the internet, or is it entirely within our VPC?
[02:10] Samira Chen: For our Private offering, the control plane components are deployed into your VPC / private subnets. There is an option for an out-of-band control plane managed by Redwood when customers want lighter ops, but for strict security/compliance you would choose the in-VPC control plane so nothing leaves your network. In that mode all traffic stays inside your region and VPC, subject to your routing.
[02:29] Nina Alvarez: Important for us: SOC 2 scope includes audit logs for model access and request metadata. We need logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk). Is that supported?
[02:38] Samira Chen: Yes, we can push audit logs to an S3 bucket in your account or send to Kinesis/CloudWatch which you can then forward to Splunk. We also support bringing your own KMS keys for encrypting data at rest.
[02:53] Liam O'Connor: Good. On region constraints, some of our data must stay in eu-west-1. Can you deploy in that region?
[03:02] Jordan Patel: Absolutely, we support deployments in multiple regions including eu-west-1, us-east-1, us-west-2. For dedicated capacity we also have regional options. If you need specific instance types or GPU SKUs in eu-west-1, we can confirm availability — sometimes a parity issue with the newest GPUs.
[03:18] Ethan Park: Do you support self-hosted HSM/KMS or integration with our CloudHSM? We have strict key control requirements.
[03:26] Samira Chen: We integrate with customer-managed KMS keys in AWS KMS. For FIPS/HSM-level control you can bring CloudHSM and we can integrate through our stack, though there may be additional engineering work and review.
[03:38] Nina Alvarez: On the networking side, what's the expected NAT/egress behavior? We need static IPs for some vendors.
[03:46] Samira Chen: Since the inference plane runs in your VPC, egress IPs are yours — if you want static ones you should centralize egress via NAT gateways with Elastic IPs. If you're using PrivateLink, outbound calls from Redwood component toward third-party services would be through your egress unless configured otherwise.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: Are there any port requirements or security groups we should pre-provision?
[04:10] Samira Chen: We'll provide a network template. At a high level we need outbound HTTPS (443) for telemetry in some configurations, and internal ports for the gRPC/TCP traffic between our control plane and inference nodes, typically ephemeral high ports, but the template will include specifics.
[04:27] Jordan Patel: I'm going to drop a note — sample template includes subnets for control plane, inference, and optional mgmt bastion, plus recommended route table entries and NACLs.
[04:37] Ethan Park: For PrivateLink, do we still need to set up peering for model artifacts storage? We store large model blobs in S3 and we'd like Redwood to pull from our S3 buckets privately.
[04:49] Samira Chen: We support reading model artifacts from your S3 with VPC endpoints (Gateway endpoints) and IAM roles. If you prefer not to expose S3 across peering, we can push artifacts into the inference VPC via a controlled sync job that runs with cross-account role. We'll send recommended approaches — many customers use S3 Gateway endpoints in the same region.
[05:08] Nina Alvarez: About cross-account roles — are you asking us to create a role that Redwood assumes to fetch artifacts? We need audit trail for that.
[05:15] Samira Chen: Yes, typically cross-account role with least privilege. All actions are logged in CloudTrail in your account and we can include CloudTrail-based audit materials in our runbook.
[05:27] Jordan Patel: Timeline — what are you aiming for? Proof-of-concept or pilot?
[05:31] Liam O'Connor: We'd like to run a POC in Q1, ideally January. Next month is procurement gating but we'd like to lock a pilot and run throughput/latency benchmarks.
[05:40] Jordan Patel: That sounds feasible. Pilot would typically be a couple of weeks, we'd bring a small model set and run throughput tests. Samira can walk through benchmark harness.
[05:50] Samira Chen: For benchmarks, we can provide a harness to replay your request distribution. We'll need sample prompt traces, token distributions, and preferred latency SLOs. Also, what concurrency are you expecting?
[06:03] Ethan Park: We're seeing bursty traffic from our app — avg 10 rps but spikes to 200 rps. Latency SLO is 150-200 ms p50 for short prompt generation workloads. Cost is also a concern; we want to balance latency with cheaper quantized models.
[06:20] Samira Chen: We can recommend quantization profiles and batching behavior. Dedicated capacity with GPU pools will give you predictable latency and throughput; Private in-VPC gives you isolation. There's a trade-off: hosted is faster to start but doesn't meet your no-internet requirement.
[06:34] Liam O'Connor: Any thoughts on model variants and fallback? We need graceful degradation if primary GPUs are saturated.
[06:42] Samira Chen: Yes, we support routing policies and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or lower-quality configs when capacity is constrained. We can set canary rollouts and A/B as well.
[06:54] Nina Alvarez: Security question: Do you persist logs or request payloads outside our account? We need to ensure PII doesn't leak and if it does, we control retention.
[07:04] Jordan Patel: In Private in-VPC mode, data and logs can remain in your account and S3 buckets you control. For hosted mode we retain logs per our policy, but that doesn't apply here. We'll document retention options and encryption with your KMS.
[07:18] Ethan Park: What about network latency inside region? If Redwood inference components are in our VPC, the only added latency is intra-AZ networking, right?
[07:26] Samira Chen: Correct; if everything is inside your VPC and you place inference nodes in the same AZs as your app, network latency is minimal. We suggest pinning subnets per AZ to reduce cross-AZ hops.
[07:38] Liam O'Connor: Is there a recommended instance family for inference? We're leaning toward A100s in a dedicated pool, but cost is high. Any recommendations for balanced latency/cost?
[07:48] Samira Chen: A100 is premium latency; you can also use H100 or 4-bit quantized models on NVIDIA T4s or similar for much lower cost. We will include recommended SKU mapping per model in the architecture doc.
[07:59] Jordan Patel: Quick question — any constraints on outbound IP allowlists? You mentioned some partners require static egress.
[08:06] Nina Alvarez: We maintain an allowlist for partner webhooks; we'll need to know what egress IPs Redwood would use if any traffic leaves our VPC. But if everything runs in our VPC there should be none.
[08:17] Samira Chen: Right — if fully in-VPC, outbound is your egress. If you opt for a managed egress or Redwood-hosted components, we'll provide a small set of egress IPs.
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: Ok. Can you share a sample architecture diagram and Terraform templates?
[08:32] Jordan Patel: Absolutely. We'll send an architecture doc, a network template (Terraform), and a pricing matrix for dedicated vs private options.
[08:40] Ethan Park: On procurement, what's the typical contract model for Private? Monthly reserved capacity or committed annual?
[08:47] Jordan Patel: We offer both monthly reserved and annual commits for Dedicated/Private. For pilots, we often do a short-term trial with a small reserved bucket. We'll outline options in the pricing sheet.
[08:57] Nina Alvarez: One more security nuance — we need to ensure that the control plane components don't have access to plaintext secrets. Can we ensure sidecar or secrets never leave our control?
[09:06] Samira Chen: We support in-VPC deployments where secrets are stored in customer KMS and only decrypted in your environment. We have a secrets handling guide; we'll include it.
[09:16] Jordan Patel: Cool. Recap and next steps: We'll send the architecture doc, Terraform template, pricing matrix, and propose a technical deep dive with your security team next week. You (Nina) will send CIDR ranges and transit gateway info; Liam will confirm target pilot timeline in Jan.
[09:32] Liam O'Connor: Yep, I'll confirm pilot scope with procurement and get back by Friday. Nina will send network details.
[09:39] Nina Alvarez: I'll compile the CIDRs and compliance checklist by Wednesday.
[09:44] Jordan Patel: Great — action items noted. Samira, anything to add?
[09:47] Samira Chen: I'll follow up with the sample benchmark harness and example network configs.
[09:52] Ethan Park: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:55] Jordan Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive. Bye.
[42:00] End of recording

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'K V cache' heard as 'K V cash' in places; names sometimes mis-tagged by auto-transcript. References: architecture doc (link: /redwood/private/arch-cygnus.pdf), terraform template (link: /redwood/private/terraform-cygnus.zip), pricing spreadsheet (link: /redwood/pricing/cygnus-pilot.xlsx).
